keyword: what is fisa in the government
claims: The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) of 1978 is a U.S. federal law.
FISA establishes procedures for physical and electronic surveillance of foreign intelligence information.
FISA allows government agencies like the NSA and FBI to conduct surveillance on foreign powers and agents without traditional warrants.
FISA was created to regulate surveillance aimed at collecting foreign intelligence rather than criminal evidence.
The FISA Court (FISC) is a specialized federal court that reviews government applications for surveillance orders.
Section 702 of FISA allows the government to compel U.S. companies to provide data on non-U.S. persons located outside the U.S.
FISA is overseen by all three branches.
FISA was enacted after intelligence abuses were revealed in the 1970s.
FISA has been amended by the FISA Amendments Act of 2008.
